title: Rhythm
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 1 Creative Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Walk to a drum beat first. Body percussion: clap, tap knees, snap, stamp, one at a time.

skills.key_step: The child names things that keep a steady pulse and tells a steady beat from uneven sounds.
steps: Is it even? Then it is a steady beat.

board.do: Walk and count 1, 2, 1, 2 with the drum.
Does a clock tick like this?
Yes: a clock keeps a steady beat.

misconceptions.ask: Does rain on the roof keep a steady beat?
misconceptions.repair: Clap with a clock tick, then try to clap with the rain.

misconceptions.ask: When you keep a steady beat, does it get faster?
misconceptions.repair: Walk to the drum: do your feet speed up?

misconceptions.ask: Which keeps a steady beat: a ticking clock or people talking?
misconceptions.repair: Clap with talking, then with a clock.

misconceptions.ask: Can a soft sound keep a steady beat?
misconceptions.repair: Tap a steady beat softly with one finger.

checks.question: Does a ticking clock keep a steady beat?
Does rain keep a steady beat?

skills.key_step: The child names clapping, tapping, snapping and stamping and the body parts that make them, and keeps the beat of a song with them.
steps: Play it on the beat of the song.

misconceptions.ask: You rub your thumb and finger to make a click. What is that?
misconceptions.repair: Clap, then snap, and look at the hands.

misconceptions.ask: Which body part do you stamp with?
Can you play percussion with only your body?
misconceptions.repair: Play a song with claps and stamps only.

misconceptions.ask: When you clap along to a song, when do you clap?
misconceptions.repair: Walk and clap together with the song.

checks.question: Name two body percussion sounds.
checks.answer: any two of: clap, tap, snap, stamp

checks.question: Which body part do you stamp with?
